Triage: **outcome 2, measured.** The rule over-reaches; the fix lands in `packages/lint/src/validate-widget-bindings.ts` ⇒ `domain:devx`. Graded `Bug` · `priority:p2`.

Triage seat, session `session_01SwJQDFKe8tVit3BXQ9EfR5`, R+145, 2026-09-04T15:20Z.

### The card asked for a reading on objectui's side. Here it is

The card is explicit that deciding needs someone to look at what `DatasetWidget` does with a `chartConfig`-less pie. Read on objectui `origin/main` at 15:18Z — and the renderer states its own contract in pinned test names, so this is a contract reading rather than an inference:

| `packages/plugin-dashboard/src/__tests__/DatasetWidget.chartConfig.test.tsx` | |
|:--|:--|
| `:179` | *"ignores an authored axis `field` and **keeps the derived axis binding**"* |
| `:192` | *"ignores an authored series and **keeps one derived series per measure**"* |
| `:204` | *"ignores `chartConfig.type` — the widget type owns the chart family"* |
| `:159` | *"emits none of the presentation keys when no chartConfig is declared"* |

And `DatasetWidget.tsx`'s own header (`:19`): the chart family is drawn *"with its TRUE chart type and **one series per measure**"*.

⇒ **The axis binding and the series are DERIVED from the widget's `dimensions` / `values`.** An authored `chartConfig.xAxis.field` is not merely optional — it is actively **refused**. `chartConfig` carries presentation only: titles, height, colours, data labels, annotations, legend.

⇒ The rule's stated consequence — *"the renderer cannot determine which measure to plot, so the series renders empty"* — is **false against that renderer**. The two `system_overview` widgets are valid metadata, and `chart-config-missing` is producing a false finding on them. That is precisely the ADR-0072 D1 cost the card names, and the repair belongs in the rule.

⚠️ **What this reading does ⛔ not establish**, and the devx seat should close it before editing: I read objectui's `origin/main`, which is the published-package side. The Console renders these dashboards through whatever `@object-ui/*` version it pins, and I have ⛔ not checked that the pinned version derives the same way. The derivation is pinned by name in tests rather than incidental, so it is unlikely to differ — but "unlikely" is not measured, and the rule's exemption should be written against the behaviour the shipped pin actually has.

### Grading

`domain:devx` — `packages/lint` is squarely in that lane, and the landing file is `validate-widget-bindings.ts`. ⛔ Not `domain:engine`: the dashboard source in `packages/platform-objects` is the *symptom's* location, and symptom location does not set routing. Had outcome 1 been the answer, this would have been `domain:engine` instead — which is exactly why the card was worth measuring rather than routing on where the warning pointed.

`Bug` by the mechanical boundary test — the accept set does not widen; a rule is brought back into agreement with the behaviour it claims to describe.

`priority:p2` rather than p3: a warning-tier rule that mis-fires on **first-party shipped metadata** is the fastest way to train every reader, human and agent, that this rule family is noise. The card's own sentence is the case — *"a permanent advisory on every build hides the next real one"* — and the exemption is bounded, so the cost of leaving it is larger than the cost of fixing it.

### Shape of the work, ⛔ not a fence

Exempt the shape the renderer demonstrably derives, rather than deleting the rule: a widget whose chart family and series the renderer derives from `dimensions` / `values` does not need `chartConfig` to plot. ⚠️ The rule may still have a true arm — if some widget shape genuinely cannot be derived, that arm should survive with a message that names the real consequence. Whether such a shape exists is a measurement, ⛔ not assumed here in either direction.
